news.title: Football-mad teen earns Norwich City deal after returning from World Cup
news.lede: From the World Cup stage to Carrow Road, teenage footballer Rylan Heaney is living out the football dream he has chased since he could walk. The 15-year-old, from Beccles, has returned from Azerbaijan after representing Northern Ireland at the FIFA U15 World Cup, helping his side finish 27th out of 193 teams. After being selected through his family ties to the country, Rylan attended a national training camp before heading to his first World Cup, an experience he described as unforgettable. Rylan Heaney representing Northern Ireland at the U15 FIFA World Cup in Azerbaijan, where he competed against teams from around the world (Image: Supplied).

news.title: Injured Trinity Rodman to miss USWNT’s FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 qualifier vs El Salvador
news.lede: CHENNAI Forward Trinity Rodman will not be available for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT) for an upcoming qualifying tournament for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 due to a minor shoulder injury. The 24-year-old Rodman sustained the knock on Saturday early during Washington Spirit’s 2-1 defeat against Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship ‌Game -- the Spirit’s third consecutive loss in the title match. Rodman was challenging for a ball when Current defender Laney ‌Rouse ⁠sent her hard into the ground after a mid-air collision. After being off the field for several minutes during which she met the trainers, she returned to the game.

news.title: NSA congratulates Black Challenge after historic Amputee World Cup triumph
news.lede: Ghana's National Sports Authority (NSA) has congratulated the Black Challenge after the national amputee football team made history by winning the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The Black Challenge secured Ghana's first-ever world title in amputee football after defeating Morocco 1-0 in the final on Sunday, 22 November, in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. Captain Richard Opentil scored the decisive goal in the 32nd minute as Ghana overcame their North African opponents to claim the trophy. The victory also made Ghana only the second African country to win the competition, following Angola's success in 2018.

news.title: A hero's welcome: Amputee football team home after historic World Cup silver medal
news.lede: Morocco’s national amputee football team received an official and public welcome at Rabat-Salé Airport late Tuesday, following its historic second-place finish at the 2026 World Cup in Mexico. The team secured the silver medal after reaching the final against Ghana, marking the first time a Moroccan national amputee football team had reached a World Cup final. The delegation was welcomed by Minister Delegate for Social Inclusion Rachid Hamouni, players’ families and Moroccan supporters, including members of the Sbouaa ultras and representatives of the Nahdat Agadir amputee football team. Speaking to Hespress, Hamouni congratulated the players on behalf of the government and praised the efforts of the medical and technical staff, as well as all members of the federation.

news.title: Football: Eleventh for Jackson and England at WAFF World Cup
news.lede: Isle of Man footballer, Sean Jackson and the England amputee national football squad have finished 11th at this year's WAFF World Cup in Mexico. The national side secured their final position in this year's event following a 2-1 victory in their final play-off contest against Costa Rica on Sunday (22 November). It follows a campaign in which the England side topped Group F with two wins and one draw to reach the knockout phase. That was followed by a 2-1 loss to Egypt in the Last-16 stage which saw England move into the final play-off contests.
